content.comment_body: I need to measure temperatures up to 350°C with PT100/1000 sensors, but the [product_name] datasheet shows a measurement range of only -50 to +200°C. Is this strictly enforced, or is it simply the range guaranteed to be within tolerance?

The [product_name] is built to evaluate PT100/1000 sensors only within -50°C to 200°C, and these limits can't be adjusted. If you require measurements up to 350°C or higher, you'll need external PT transducers providing 0-10V or 0/4-20mA outputs. If your main module lacks analog inputs, an additional [product_name] is necessary. Note: Wider measurement ranges reduce resolution. For instance, with a 0 to 400°C range, 400°C/1000 units equals 0.4°C per unit of resolution.

This restriction feels arbitrary. A comparable module from another vendor offers 4 channels and supports -200 to +850°C for PT100 sensors. Even a [version_no] RTD module allows this wider range. However, I need a local display and web interface, which [product_name] provides at a very competitive price. It seems this limitation is intentionally imposed by [company_name]. Thankfully, I only need a 2-degree accuracy at 350°C, which isn't an issue.
I'm not sure if it's an arbitrary restriction, but I doubt that's the case. Also, you don't have to use an [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unhappy with the limited temperature measurement range of the [product_name] for PT100/PT1000 sensors. The module supports only -50 to +200°C and can't be modified, which restricts its usability. This limitation seems unnecessarily restrictive compared to other hardware options from both competitors and [company_name], especially since users appreciate the product's cost and its display/web features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the [product_name] to support broader temperature ranges for PT100/1000 sensors, ideally up to 350°C, consistent with competitor and standard offerings. They hope for greater flexibility and fewer design limits for practical industrial applications.
